common:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: one individual orthographic turnaround reference for Tripo multi-view reconstruction, NOT a concept redesign and NOT a contact sheet. Input image is the exact FRONT view of the SAME adult male low-poly soldier; preserve identity, full-body proportions, broad chest, thick coat and sleeves, helmet dimensions, angular armour, scarf, blue-gray tall collar, dark trousers, gloves, black calf-high boots, muted slate-blue and olive palette, simple large flat facets. NO weapons, backpack, bedroll, goggles, crystals, antennas, wires, yellow patch or new equipment.
Same static A-pose in 3D: arms straight 45 degrees below horizontal in the torso's frontal plane, hands empty and relaxed, legs straight with shoulder-width foot spacing. Rotate only the camera around him; do not change the pose. Head remains aligned with torso; never turns toward camera.
Use the exact same 1024 x 1536 portrait canvas and orthographic scale as the supplied front. Helmet top at y=33 pixels, boot sole baseline y=1478 pixels, centered on x=512. Match shoulder, belt, coat hem and knee heights to the front reference. Do not zoom to fill the narrower silhouette. All head, gloves and boots fully in frame. Plain uniform light warm gray background, soft even neutral illumination, no floor/cast shadow, no text, labels or watermark.
There is ONE white four-diamond insignia on the soldier's ANATOMICAL LEFT shoulder (on image-right in the supplied front). Right shoulder is plain charcoal. Preserve that asymmetry correctly, not mirrored. Olive front webbing continues as two simple shoulder straps down the back to the belt; no new back armour or backpack. Coat is plain slate blue at back with one simple center back hem vent. Helmet ivory stripe runs front-to-back over the center of the crown.

The camera is directly on the soldier's ANATOMICAL LEFT SIDE, so the LEFT shoulder with the white four-diamond insignia is the near visible shoulder. One eye at most in profile, no front face, no three-quarter shoulders or view into the chest plate's front. Coat thickness and helmet brim must be consistent with both supplied references.

Arms extend sideways out of the torso's frontal plane toward/away from the camera and downward, not forwards or backwards. In an exact side projection the near and far arms align and overlap, with the nearest hand projected by the side of the upper thigh at the SAME hand height as the front reference. Do not show the A silhouette by moving the arms in the sagittal plane. Near and far legs and boots likewise overlap at the same baseline; don't spread them front-to-back. No bent elbows or knees. Only one narrow side silhouette, maintaining the full front image's vertical scale.
left_correction:
Precise single-detail correction to this LEFT-SIDE orthographic profile. Preserve the complete image pixel-for-pixel as closely as possible: same character, same profile facing image-left, same pose, silhouette, armour, left shoulder insignia, colour palette, dimensions, background and placement.
Correct ONLY the helmet's painted stripe. The wide vertical ivory stripe currently painted across the side face of the helmet is incorrect. The ivory identification stripe belongs on the CENTER sagittal ridge, running from the forehead over the crown to the back of the head. In this exact SIDE view the large side panel of the helmet must therefore be entirely uniform slate-blue, with at most a tiny thin ivory edge visible along the very top ridge. Remove the big ivory stripe from the helmet side and replace it with the same flat blue polygon shading as the adjacent helmet panels. Do not rotate the helmet or redraw the soldier. No other edits.
